claims.claim: ὑποτασσόμεναι is a present middle/passive participle, nominative feminine plural, from ὑποτάσσω.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: The Sarah clause has a clear textual/narrative anchor in Gen 18:12 LXX, where Sarah calls Abraham 'my lord'.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: Greco-Roman moral discourse contains both household asymmetry and ideals of marital companionship/consideration; a single uniform marriage model is unsafe.
claims.limitations: Limited inspection/reconstruction remains; do not promote to fact.

claims.claim: The passage explicitly envisages at least some wives whose husbands disobey the word; scholarship often studies this as a mixed-belief marriage setting.
claims.limitations: Limited inspection/reconstruction remains; do not promote to fact.

claims.claim: ἀσθενεστέρῳ is morphologically a comparative adjective modifying σκεύει; 'physically weaker', 'socially vulnerable', or a combined account is exegetical, not morphology.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The text calls wives συγκληρονόμοις of the grace of life and instructs husbands to apportion honor.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: Whether the household material is best characterized as accommodation, apologetic strategy, subversion, or a mixed strategy is debated in scholarship.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: 1 Peter 3:10-12 is a sustained quotation/adaptation of Ps 33:13-17 LXX (Ps 34:12-16 in common English/MT numbering).
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: The sequence 'do not fear ... nor be troubled' and 'sanctify the Lord' is clear verbal reuse/adaptation of Isa 8:12-13 LXX.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: Peter's adapted wording places τὸν Χριστόν with κύριον in the Isaiah-shaped exhortation, a textually significant Christological reuse.
claims.limitations: Limited inspection/reconstruction remains; do not promote to fact.

claims.claim: ἁγιάσατε is aorist active imperative, second plural, from ἁγιάζω; ἀπολογίαν is an accusative singular noun.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: The inspected SBLGNT/MorphGNT text reads ἔπαθεν ('suffered'), not a Greek verb meaning 'died', in the opening clause of 3:18.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: The referent/force of σαρκί ... πνεύματι (spheres/aspects, human spirit, Holy Spirit, etc.) is exegetically disputed.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: 1 Enoch preserves a Second Temple Watchers tradition linking Noah-era judgment with rebellious heavenly beings bound in darkness awaiting judgment.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: The identity of the 'spirits in prison' is contested: serious readings include Noah's human contemporaries and rebellious/demonic spirits associated with the Noah/Genesis 6 complex.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The timing and content of ἐκήρυξεν are disputed: pre-incarnate preaching through Noah, postmortem/descent readings, and post-resurrection victory proclamation are distinct options.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The text explicitly says that a few, 'that is, eight souls', were brought safely through water in the Noah episode.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: In the inspected Greek, ἀντίτυπον is nominative neuter singular, βάπτισμα is nominative neuter singular, and σῴζει is present active indicative third singular.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: ἐπερώτημα is morphologically a nominative neuter singular noun; its contextual sense is disputed among question/answer, appeal/request, and pledge/commitment readings.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The statement 'baptism now saves you' is qualified by a contrast with removal of bodily dirt and by reference to a good conscience/ἐπερώτημα and Jesus Christ's resurrection.
claims.limitations: Serious alternatives remain; keep noncompetitive.

claims.claim: The text presents Christ as gone into heaven, at God's right hand, with angels, authorities, and powers subjected to him.
claims.limitations: Bounded inspected claim only; no downstream inference is implied.

claims.claim: 1 Peter directly depends literarily on 1 Enoch's Book of the Watchers.
claims.limitations: Inspected evidence does not prove this claim.

claims.claim: ἐπερώτημα lexically means 'pledge', therefore 1 Peter 3:21 cannot mean 'appeal'.
claims.limitations: Rejected: certainty exceeds inspected evidence.

claims.claim: The SBLGNT Greek text of 1 Peter 3:18 says that Christ 'died' for sins.
claims.limitations: Rejected: certainty exceeds inspected evidence.

do_not_claim: Do not claim every wife in 3:1-6 had an unbelieving husband; the text says some.
Do not claim 3:1-7 commands a wife to remain in domestic violence; that is not a direct textual fact.
Do not make 'weaker vessel' one settled physical/social/moral sense from morphology.
Do not turn one Greco-Roman witness into universal Asia-Minor marriage law or practice.
Do not call 3:10-12 mechanically verbatim Psalm 34; it is sustained quotation/adaptation.
Do not reduce Isaiah 8:12-13 in 3:14-15 to a vague parallel, or make morphology prove full Christology.
Do not say the inspected SBLGNT of 3:18 reads 'died'; it reads ἔπαθεν.
Do not settle σαρκί/πνεύματι in 3:18 from morphology alone.
Do not claim 'spirits in prison' certainly means fallen angels, human dead, or Noah's contemporaries.
Do not make ἐκήρυξεν itself prove gospel invitation or only judgment/victory.
Do not claim direct dependence on 1 Enoch from Watchers/Noah parallels alone.
Do not claim ἐπερώτημα means only pledge or only appeal.
Do not prove or disprove baptismal regeneration by lexical fiat in 3:21.
Do not claim all conservative interpreters agree on 3:19-21.
Do not infer empire-wide official persecution from chapter 3 alone.

positions: degree and formulation of resulting Christological inference requires further argument
preincarnate Christ preaching through Noah to humans (Grudem)
post-resurrection victory proclamation to demonic/fallen spirits (MacArthur/Schreiner)
descent/postmortem human-spirit readings in wider history

status_policy.VERIFIED: Direct inspected evidence supports the bounded claim.
status_policy.PARTIAL: Useful support exists, but part of the claim depends on limited inspection or reconstruction.
status_policy.CONTESTED: Materially different serious interpretations remain live.
status_policy.HOLD: Inspected evidence does not warrant publication as fact.
status_policy.REJECTED_OVERCLAIM: The proposed certainty exceeds or contradicts inspected evidence.
